visibility.description: internal: only internal viewers can see the map. all-users: signed-in users see the customer-facing view.

customer.description: Customer-facing map title and summary. Required when visibility is all-users.

title.description: Customer-facing title. Add only after the wording is approved.

stalledAfterWeeks.description: Flag a story as stalled when it has been in progress for longer than this many weeks. Defaults to 4. 0 turns the flag off. Needs the history file from `story-map history`.

plans.description: Whether this product keeps delivery plans: the repository-relative folder they go in, such as docs/plans, or false for no plans. Leave it out until a person has chosen, and validate asks for the choice. Set it with `story-map settings --plans`. See Write a delivery plan in docs/story-map.md.

storyIds.description: How `story-map add` numbers a new story when --id is left out. next, the default, takes one after the highest number. lowest-free takes the lowest unused number above the lowest one in use. Both use the prefix most stories have and count cut stories, so an ID is never reused.

settings.description: Optional settings for everyone who views the map. Hosts can override them.

personas.description: Optional. Up to 12 people the product serves, with their jobs to be done.

id.description: Stable persona ID that stories reference in their personas. Keep it when renaming.

title.description: Internal persona name, such as “Product manager”. The board takes the avatar's initials from it.

summary.description: Optional internal summary of who they are and what they own.

context.description: Optional internal context: what success means to them, what they use today and their constraints. Never shown to customers.

success.description: Optional. What a good result looks like to them, such as “Weekly forecast accuracy, judged by the VP of Sales” or “Every bill paid on time”.

usesToday.description: Optional. Up to 8 products, tools and workarounds they rely on now, which a story competes with.

constraints.description: Optional. Up to 6 constraints they work under, which change what a story can assume.

draft.description: true when an agent drafted this context and nobody has confirmed it yet. Only a person removes it.

jobs.description: Optional. Up to 8 jobs to be done that stories serve. The first is the persona's core job, the one that matters most, so reordering the jobs changes it.

id.description: Stable job ID, unique across the map, that stories reference in their jobs. Keep it when rewording the job or moving it to another persona.

situation.description: Written without its lead word, which the board adds: “When …”. The trigger and what makes it hard, not only the moment or a role. Such as “a release is being planned and its scope is spread across chat threads and tickets”.

motivation.description: Written without its lead word, which the board adds: “I want …”. What they want to do in that moment, in their words, without naming a feature. Such as “to agree its scope in the PR that changes the map”.

outcome.description: Written without its lead word, which the board adds: “so that …”. What gets better for them and what is at stake if it does not. Such as “engineers and product start from the same list, rather than finding out at the demo that they meant different things”.

draft.description: true when an agent drafted this job and nobody has confirmed it yet. Only a person removes it.

steps.description: Optional. Up to 6 workflow steps, in order, each pointing to the activity where its stories live. Any job can have steps, not only the core job.

title.description: A short name for the step, up to 60 characters, such as “Gather” or “Agree scope”.

summary.description: Optional. What the persona does in this step.

activity.description: Optional ID of the activity where the stories for this step live. The step's stories are those that serve its job and sit in this activity. A step without one has no stories of its own.

items.description: One step of a job, in the order the persona does them. Internal only.
A job to be done: “When <situation>, I want <motivation>, so that <outcome>.” Internal only.

customer.description: Customer-facing persona name. Add only after the wording is approved.

title.description: Customer-facing title. Add only after the wording is approved.

items.description: A person the product serves. The order sets each persona's colour on the board.

id.description: Stable activity ID that stories reference. Keep it when renaming.

customer.description: Customer-facing activity label. Required before a customer-facing story can use this activity.

title.description: Customer-facing title. Add only after the wording is approved.

items.description: Activities run left to right in the order of the user journey.

id.description: Stable release ID that stories reference. Keep it when renaming.

customer.description: Customer-facing release label. Required before a customer-facing story can use this release.

title.description: Customer-facing title. Add only after the wording is approved.

notes.description: Optional internal release notes: plain text up to 800 characters. Blank lines separate paragraphs. No Markdown.

impact.description: Optional, recommended. Up to 10 expected outcomes of the release. Internal only.

metric.description: What is measured, such as “Estimate turnaround time”.

expected.description: The expected change, written for people, such as “Decrease from 3 days to 1 day”. Not parsed.

actual.description: Optional. The measured result, added after shipping.

draft.description: true when an agent drafted this item and nobody has confirmed it yet. Only a person removes it.

items.description: Releases run top to bottom in delivery order.

id.description: Stable story ID, such as BUILDER-102. Keep it when renaming or moving the story.

activity.description: ID of the activity column this story sits under.

release.description: ID of the release lane this story belongs to.

summary.description: Optional internal summary, shown when the card is opened.

status.description: planned: agreed work awaiting implementation. in-progress: work has started. merged: the work is merged to the default branch but not yet available to its intended users; customers see it as in progress. shipped: available to its intended users. blocked: started or agreed, but cannot continue. cut: deliberately dropped from its release. Blocked and cut stories are hidden by default and never shown to customers.

statusReason.description: Why the story is blocked or cut. Internal only.

jobs.description: Optional. Up to 4 job IDs, most important first. The story's personas include the persona that owns each job.

personas.description: Optional. Up to 4 persona IDs, most important first. For a persona the story helps without serving one of their jobs. Personas from jobs need not be repeated.

dependsOn.description: Optional. Up to 10 IDs of stories that must land before this one, most important first. Internal only. The stories waiting for a story are worked out from these lists, so list each dependency once, on the story that waits.

estimate.description: Optional effort estimate in story points: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. Internal only. A story above 13 should be split.

priority.description: Optional MoSCoW priority: must, should or could have. Internal only. The board shows it as an MH, SH or CH tag.

tokens.description: Optional. Model tokens used to deliver the story, counting input, output and cache tokens, recorded in the pull request that finishes it, such as from `story-map tokens`. Internal only.

estimatedCostUsd.description: Optional. Estimated cost of those tokens in US dollars at API list prices, such as from `story-map tokens`. Internal only. It is not what was billed: a subscription, discount or another provider changes that.

updatedBy.description: Optional. Display name of the person to credit for this edit, when it is not the commit author. The status history credits Git otherwise.

sources.description: Supporting docs, tests or links. The first Markdown link with a #heading becomes the Engineering overview link.

customer.description: Customer-facing copy. Add only when the story is approved for all users.

title.description: Customer-facing title. Add only after the wording is approved.

items.description: Stories appear in this order within each cell.

title: Auto Story Map
description: A Git-backed user story map. Validate cross-references with `story-map validate`.
